source.description: The documented rules R1-R15 of Rule Sabotage V6.1 as listed by gamewatch/rules-doc.ts and recorded as game.rules in the evidence bundle (spec partition: spec/spec.json). Each record is bound to its rule text by SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text.
source.game: Rule Sabotage V6.1 (13x9 board, no new effects next to any piece)

encodingAuthor.version: GW2 P5 thread draft, 2026-11-25 (encoding-1 records R3, R7, R8, R14 unchanged; R5 and R12 added under Q22 limited scope)

review.note: Q3: provisional until independently reviewed and accepted by the operator. Not an authoritative reference for confirmatory experiments. The encoding is itself a challengeable artifact: a challenge is a graph node that references this file by hash.

records.reason: Board geometry, start squares and scoring are not represented by the P4 situation kinds (no movement or scoring situation).
Turn alternation, game end and tie-breaks need game-level situations that P4 does not extract.

records.supportedScope: Turn starts only: the number of move actions granted at the start of a turn (actionsGranted) from the own pieces on the board and the extra actions earned for that turn.
limitations: "One move action per own piece still on the board" is read as the count of own pieces on a board square at the turn start; frozen pieces are counted (R11 does not say they grant no action). This reading is the encoder's.

"+1 action" effects earned during the opponent's turn are counted through recorded extra-action events (thisTurn=false) since the side's previous turn start; extra actions for the current turn (thisTurn=true) are not part of actionsGranted and are not checked.
What an action may move (one piece or a whole stack, one square orthogonally) is not encoded.

records.reason: Stacking and capture need movement situations that P4 does not extract.

records.supportedScope: Scripted placement attempts (effect-placement situations): a placement with a chosen cell on one of the 8 squares around any piece, or on a cell holding a piece or an enemy effect, is refused.
limitations: Only the refusal direction is encoded: a placement that breaks neither condition may still be refused by the referee (R6) and the encoding makes no prediction for it.
"Before the first move of a turn", "ONE effect" per turn, 1 to 3 cells and removal of own effects are not encoded.
nearAnyPiece and cellOccupied are derived from the before-state of the placement step; match rows have no board state, so only scripted cases are evaluated.

records.reason: The referee procedure is not an observable outcome of a single situation.

records.supportedScope: Effect entries recorded with board states (scripted cases): entries that agree on effect kind, arrival, whether the piece was shielded and whether the chain cap applied must have the same observable outcome (fired, absorbed, cell used up, shield afterwards) whichever side owns the piece and whichever side owns the effect.
limitations: Only these four outcome fields are compared; where the piece ends up, the direction of a shove, freeze duration and who receives a "+1 action" are not compared.
Effect kinds are compared as a class (all shoves together), which is appropriate only for the four compared outcome fields.
Requires pieceShieldedBefore, which match rows do not record, so matches do not contribute.
The direction sentence of R7 (absolute or relative directions) is not encoded.

records.supportedScope: Effect entries that are not past the chain cap: the entered cell is used up afterwards, by own move or forced arrival; an unshielded piece sets the effect off; the other cells of a multi-cell effect stay.
limitations: The chain cap (R9) is taken from the recorded chain-limit event; entries past the cap are excluded rather than checked.
A shielded entry is left to R14 for whether the effect fires; R8 is still checked for the cell being used up, as R14 states.
cellUsedUp and otherCellsRemain need board states, so only scripted cases contribute; when the same cell is entered twice in one step the outcome is unknown and excluded.

records.reason: The chain cap itself is not checked (it would need the chain length per arrival); R8 uses the recorded chain-limit event as an input.
Shove distances and directions need movement outcomes that P4 does not extract.
Freeze duration needs move-refusal situations that P4 does not extract.

records.supportedScope: Entries of an unshielded piece on a Send home cell, not past the chain cap: the effect fires and the piece is moved back to its start square.
limitations: "Goes back to its start square" is read as a forced-move event with how "home" for the entering piece after the entry; the destination square itself is not compared with the start square.
Entries of shielded pieces are left to R14; entries past the chain cap to R9 (unencoded).
In match rows pieceShieldedBefore is unknown, so only scripted cases are evaluated.

records.reason: Teleport destinations are random; no P4 situation represents them.

records.supportedScope: Effect entries by a piece that was shielded before entering (scripted cases), not past the chain cap: the effect does not apply (absorbed, not fired), the shield is used up, and the cell is used up.
limitations: "The effect does not apply" is read as: a shield-absorbed event and no effect-fired event for that entry. Side effects of the effect itself are not inspected.
Entering a Shield cell while already shielded is covered literally (the shielded piece ignores it); the text does not say otherwise.
pieceShieldedBefore is derived from the board state before the step and recorded shield events; it is unknown (excluded) after an entry that fired on a shielded piece in the same step.
"Gets a shield" on entering a Shield cell unshielded is not encoded.

records.reason: Who receives the extra action is not an extracted outcome; R3 uses recorded extra-action events as inputs.
